nodes.name: Dholera Industrial Node

coordinates.note: Activation-area centroid reused from app/corridors/geo.ts (verified plus-code, Aug 2026).

nodes.headline: India’s only approved commercial logic fab sits in a node whose road link has arrived, whose airport is close, and whose rail link is five years out.
strategic_overview: Dholera’s industrial identity is set by one anchor: the Tata Electronics–PSMC fab (₹91,000 crore, 50,000 wafer starts a month), approved by the Cabinet in February 2024. The September 2026 vendor-park and materials MoUs — Fujifilm’s phased materials plant inside the SIR among them — are the first sign of a supplier layer forming around it.

Connectivity is arriving out of sequence. The 109 km Ahmedabad–Dholera expressway is open for testing and cuts Ahmedabad–Dholera to about 45 minutes; the international airport next door is under construction; the semi high-speed rail line was only approved in May 2026 and runs to 2030-31. For a fab, that order matters: road moves construction material and people, but chemicals, gases and equipment spares need predictable multimodal routes, and finished wafers move by air.

Techadyant’s reading: in the near term Dholera’s competitiveness is set less by distance than by how quickly time-critical air cargo and bulk chemical logistics become dependable. That gap is also where the node’s earliest supplier opportunities sit.

nodes.name: Sanand Industrial Node

coordinates.note: Sanand town centroid; the GIDC estates lie within ~10 km.

nodes.headline: India’s first working chip-packaging cluster just gained a dedicated freight-rail station — the connectivity now runs ahead of the supplier base.
strategic_overview: Sanand is where India’s semiconductor mission first produced output. Micron’s ATMP (outlay above ₹22,500 crore) began commercial production in February 2026; Kaynes Semicon followed in March, and CG Semi (with Renesas and Stars Microelectronics) moved from a pilot line toward commercial production during 2026 — the MeitY Secretary described all three as in commercial production in August.

The connectivity profile is the strongest of the pilot nodes. Ahmedabad’s international airport is about 30 km away, an older national highway runs through the town, and on 8 September 2026 the Western DFC’s New Sanand (North)–New Makarpura section was dedicated, completing the freight corridor to JNPA.

Techadyant’s reading: Sanand’s constraint is no longer transport but depth — packaging materials, substrates, gases and test services are still largely imported. Linde’s new packaging-gas site is the first visible move. With rail freight in place, the question becomes whether consolidated, specialised logistics will form around three running OSATs.

nodes.name: Jewar–YEIDA Industrial Node

coordinates.note: YEIDA Sector 28 lies near Noida International Airport; point placed near the airport (±10 km).

nodes.headline: An OSAT being built beside a new cargo airport — the rare Indian node where air logistics arrives before the factory.
strategic_overview: The HCL–Foxconn joint venture (India Chip) was approved in May 2025 to package display-driver chips — 20,000 wafers a month and 36 million units a month — near Jewar airport in the YEIDA area, on a site moved to Sector 28 to avoid land delays. Groundbreaking was in February 2026.

Noida International Airport’s first phase was inaugurated in March 2026 with an integrated cargo terminal and logistics zones, and its first cargo flight landed in June 2026. The Western DFC terminus and the Dadri multimodal hub (under construction) sit roughly 40 km north.

Techadyant’s reading: Jewar inverts the usual sequence. Air cargo — the mode that matters most for chip packaging — is operational before the OSAT ships anything. Seaports are far, so the node’s competitiveness will rest on air and on DFC-linked inland logistics rather than on coastal access.

nodes.name: Jagiroad Industrial Node
nodes.headline: India’s largest planned OSAT sits ~85 km from the nearest cargo airport and ~580 km from the nearest seaport — the pilot that tests the gap model.
strategic_overview: Tata Semiconductor Assembly and Test (TSAT) was approved in February 2024 at ₹27,000 crore with capacity of up to 48 million chips a day, using flip-chip and integrated-system-in-package technologies. Assam’s Chief Minister said in September 2026 that operations are scheduled to start in December 2026.

Jagiroad sits on NH-27 and on the electrified Guwahati–Lumding rail line, about 85 km straight-line from Guwahati’s airport, which handles international cargo through AAICLAS while a new international cargo terminal is still listed as upcoming. The nearest seaport (Kolkata) is roughly 580 km away straight-line, and the dedicated freight corridors end well to the west.

Techadyant’s reading: Jagiroad’s economics depend on air freight and on how well Guwahati’s cargo capacity scales. Every material input arrives over long distances, which makes the node a strong candidate for local consolidation, maintenance and consumables supply — and the clearest test of whether a strategic anchor can pull logistics investment into a peripheral node.

nodes.name: Sriperumbudur–Oragadam Electronics Belt

coordinates.note: Sriperumbudur town centroid (public gazetteer); Oragadam lies to the south. Not a site boundary.

nodes.headline: India’s densest electronics-assembly belt sits within ~50 km of two major ports and an international cargo airport — the test of whether gateway proximity is already priced in.
strategic_overview: Samsung has manufactured at Sriperumbudur since 2007, and Foxconn runs an Apple-supplier SEZ plant in the SIPCOT Sriperumbudur park; a November 2024 proposal sought to expand it by 20,000 jobs. In June 2025 Foxconn was reported to be building an iPhone enclosure unit next to a display-module plant in an advanced stage of construction, in the industrial park where it holds about 500,000 sq ft at ESR Oragadam.

The belt lies roughly 25 km straight-line from Chennai’s international cargo airport and about 40 km and 50 km from Chennai Port and Kamarajar Port, both major ports. The dedicated freight corridors do not reach South India.

Techadyant’s reading: Sriperumbudur–Oragadam is gateway-rich and component-poor. The questions here are not about distance. They are about depth: whether display, enclosure and moulding capacity grows fast enough locally to cut the inbound component flow that now arrives by air and sea.

nodes.name: Kopparthy Electronics Node (YSR EMC)

coordinates.note: Approximate node location (as used in the corridor dossier map). Not a site boundary.

nodes.headline: An operating electronics cluster ~160 km straight-line from the nearest port and ~190 km from an international cargo airport — inland economics for an import-heavy industry.
strategic_overview: The 801-acre YSR Electronic Manufacturing Cluster was sanctioned under MeitY’s EMC 2.0 at ₹730 crore and sits inside APIIC’s wider Kopparthy holding on the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor. By September 2025 TechnoDom India (LED TVs), Texana World (garments) and AIL Dixon Technologies (surveillance and laptops) were operating.

The node is on NH-40/NH-67/NH-716, about 5 km from Krishnapuram station on the Chennai–Mumbai line and from Kadapa’s domestic airport. The nearest port, Krishnapatnam, is about 160 km straight-line (≈256 km by road as reported), and the nearest international cargo airport is Bengaluru, about 190 km away.

Techadyant’s reading: Kopparthy has moved from plan to production, but every imported component crosses 150–250 km of road. That favours products with high local value-add and creates a case for an inland container depot or air-cargo feeder service.
